c04.why: Every tight player has lived this exact night, the scene is complete in one sentence, and it leaves the viewer asking why it keeps happening.

c07.why: It opens on the hand the viewer is still angry about and delivers a verdict against their grievance in the same breath.

c25.why: Any player recognises both of their own wrong beliefs in it, it is a little self-mocking, and with both wrong the truth is owed.

c09.why: It names a specific beat and the feeling attached to it, so the viewer nods before deciding whether to scroll.

c11.why: It turns the viewer's own record with aces into a dare, which works on both the player who has lost with them and the one who hasn't.

c19.why: A lived moment followed by an accusation (they knew) that makes the viewer want to learn what gave them away.

c12.why: It starts with the sentence the viewer has said out loud and contradicts it at once.

c18.why: It opens on the viewer's own complaint and ends on a jab about what they paid to see those cards.

c14.why: Its last five words turn patient folding, the thing the viewer is proud of, into a cost they are paying.

c10.why: It denies luck to a viewer who blames it and then puts the fault in their own counting.
